_meta.method: structural + string/type-xref match of stripped engine funcs vs the symbol-ful stock reference; identities cross-checked with IDA (re) decompilation. Every 'found' entry is confirmed by full-body structure (slot offsets, error strings, source-line immediates, and/or being called by an already-verified caller).
_meta.verify_field: prologue16 = the function's first 16 bytes (4 arm64 instrs) as raw little-endian bytes, space-separated hex, for a runtime memcmp guard at the vmaddr. Shared frame-setup bytes across funcs are expected and harmless (the guard checks bytes AT the known vmaddr; it does not search by them).

PyDict_GetItemString.semantics: Returns a BORROWED reference into the dict; returns NULL if absent; swallows/clears any lookup error. Exactly the semantics needed for sys.modules[name]. Signature: (PyObject* dict, const char* utf8_name).

PyDict_GetItem.evidence: sub_10098DA6C(PyObject *dict, PyObject *key). The borrowed-ref getter under PyDict_GetItemString (which cross-references it: 'call PyDict_GetItem(dict,key)=sub_10098DA6C'). Returns a BORROWED reference; NULL if absent; swallows/clears any lookup error (never raises). Used by the read-only findcls/mod1 signature scan to fetch a dict value by key OBJECT without re-encoding the key (keeps the main-thread freeze budget low). NOTE: prologue16 verify intentionally omitted (address is RE-cross-referenced via GetItemString's tail call, not independently prologue-fingerprinted); the guarded symbols still gate the run and refuse a changed binary.
PyDict_GetItem.semantics: (PyObject* dict, PyObject* key) -> borrowed value or NULL, no exception on miss.

PyFloat_FromDouble.evidence: INLINED at every call site (verified in marshal r_object sub_100A76E4C, _PyFloat_Init sub_100994E7C, float_add/float___float__ sub_100996018, etc.) - LTO dead-stripped the standalone. It stores the double bits as an integer store (v[2]=bits), which is why the standalone resisted 'str d' scans. PyFloat is a non-GC 24-byte object with a dedicated free-list.
PyFloat_FromDouble.recipe: PyObject* make_float(double v): op=*(void**)0x101be9588; if(op){ *(void**)0x101be9588=*(void**)(op+8); (*(int32*)0x101be9590)--; } else { op=((void*(*)(void*,size_t))*(void**)0x101a7a668)(*(void**)0x101a7a660,24); if(!op) return 0; } *(void**)(op+8)=(void*)0x101aae5c8 /*&PyFloat_Type*/; *(intptr_t*)op=1 /*refcnt*/; *(double*)(op+0x10)=v; return op;  // (skip the flags&2 type-refcount and the 0x101c0a51c tracemalloc hook - they are debug paths, off in production)
PyFloat_FromDouble.fallback: For passing a float to setPlayRate(double), the recipe above is the cleanest. PyFloat_Type is present at 0x101aae5c8; PyNumber_Float (0x10096e65c) can normalize an existing number to a new float if you already hold a Python number.
